subject.title: [Bug]: Codex OAuth profile in main agentDir does not propagate to subagent sessions — silent fallback hallucinates tool calls in production

question: For spawned subagent runs that lose the selected Codex/OpenAI OAuth route, should OpenClaw fail closed, visibly warn and continue fallback, or keep log-only fallback after OAuth inheritance is proven?
rationale: The choice controls whether private scheduled or channel context may cross provider boundaries after an auth failure, and repository policy treats fallback behavior plus auth/provider routing as compatibility- and security-sensitive.

options.title: Require live proof and visible/fail-closed policy
options.body: Keep this issue open until a live current-main subagent run proves OAuth inheritance and define fail-closed or operator-visible behavior for auth-route loss.

options.title: Split visibility after OAuth proof
options.body: Close the propagation part only after live proof and track fallback visibility as a narrower canonical issue.

options.title: Accept log-only fallback
options.body: Keep the current structured-log fallback behavior after source proof, accepting the operator-surprise and privacy tradeoff.

recommendation.title: Require live proof and visible/fail-closed policy
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open until a live current-main subagent run proves OAuth inheritance and define fail-closed or operator-visible behavior for auth-route loss.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the central Codex OAuth ownership path and merged adjacent OAuth refresh serialization work, making them the strongest available owner for this auth/fallback boundary decision.
